evidence.source: 說文解字 online edition, reproducing Shuowen and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.field: 几 entry; glyph definition and commentary
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Shuowen’s description of 几 as a pictograph and its list of ritual furniture. Duan Yucai’s commentary corrects 踞 to 凥 and describes a raised, flat top with a support below; this is a historical interpretation, not independent proof of the graph’s original referent.
evidence.title: 说文解字：几

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry treats 𠀃 as a variant of 几 because Duan’s Shuowen entry for 且 says that the ancient form was used for both 且 and 几. This supports a variant relationship, not chronological ancestry or a ground-line interpretation.
evidence.title: [A00319] 几 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 几 entry; Shuowen and lexical references
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen gloss 踞几也 and associates 几 with the furniture entries in Guangyun. It corroborates the traditional furniture interpretation, but does not establish the character’s earliest date or a full semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「几」

evidence.text: The page reports categories for Warring States, Shuowen small seal, and Ming Liushutong forms, but this research did not inspect those glyph pixels. The claim that 𠀃 is the original form with a ground line therefore remains unsupported here; it conflicts with the MOE entry’s narrower variant classification.

evidence.text: The official site describes the glyph-evolution database as an Academia Sinica resource and reports its holdings. The specific 几 image candidate could not be verified through an accessible record and no usable direct image URL was established. No image is proposed.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org 几 Chinese character oracle bone script; 几 character ancient form table Xiaoxuetang 几 字形; 几 Shuowen 踞几也 几 variant 𠀃
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the Shuowen-derived entry, the MOE variant record, CUHK dictionary entry and secondary glyph claims. Opened source pages. Ctext returned 403; no relevant Commons file or accessible Xiaoxuetang record/direct image was established.
Search returned the official database home and general record pages but no exact usable 几 glyph record. The supplied failed image URL was not retried.

gaps: No selected glyph image: external searches and inspected pages did not establish a usable direct image with verified identity and reuse provenance. The supplied Xiaoxuetang image request had returned 401 and was excluded as required.
No glyph pixels were visually inspected. The table/stool interpretation is a traditional dictionary account; the claimed 𠀃 ground stroke and ancestor status remain unverified.

The reviewed sources do not establish a dated earliest occurrence of 几 or a chronological semantic path from stool to table. The Shuowen furniture citation is not evidence for the graph’s invention date.

No evidence supports the proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison or an object-name borrowing claim. The stool graph is treated here as an independent pictographic analysis, not as a phonetic component or demonstrated whole-graph loan.

limitations.text: No usable image candidate could be confirmed after excluding the Xiaoxuetang URL that returned HTTP 401. The MOE page supports 𠀃 as a variant, but its examined record does not offer an authorized image asset or establish an ancient chronological stage; secondary glyph tables were not visually inspected. Therefore no glyph is proposed.
